primitives.name: Blocking Constraint Satisfaction
primitives.verbatim_quote: If in the line, he must block his man long enough to make sure that the opponent cannot break through and spoil the play before it has gotten fairly started.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_{block}': 'time in seconds', 'F_{opponent}': 'force in newtons', 'd_{play}': 'distance in meters'}
primitives.assumptions: Player maintains static position until opponent breach occurs; play initiation time is deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_block < t_breach, resulting in play disruption.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a constraint optimization problem in GSI's Bayesian network where F_opponent is modeled as a stochastic variable affecting d_play.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-breach ratio and force exertion metrics.

primitives.name: Advancing Positioning Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then he must place himself, if possible, ahead of the play, where he will be in a position to help the runner, either by warding off tacklers or assisting him to shake off men who may be in the act of bringing him down.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x_{runner}': 'position vector in meters', 'x_{tackler}': 'position vector in meters', 'v_{runner}': 'velocity vector in m/s'}
primitives.assumptions: Runner trajectory is predictable; tackler proximity follows inverse distance law.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When x_runner - x_tackler < threshold, leading to collision risk.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's kernel-based motion planning model, where v_runner is optimized against x_tackler dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Distance-to-tackler ratio and velocity alignment metrics.

primitives.name: Interference Expansion Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: He should do this, of course, and after it is done, should endeavor to rejoin the runner in his course down the field, there to take care of further attack, thus making an even longer gain possible.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{gain}': 'length in meters', 'T_{rejoin}': 'time in seconds', 'P_{attack}': 'probability of continuation'}
primitives.assumptions: Rejoining path is linear; P_attack is a function of T_rejoin and L_gain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T_rejoin > T_threshold, reducing P_attack below critical value.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's sequential decision tree where P_attack is updated based on T_rejoin and L_gain outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Rejoining delay and cumulative gain metrics.

The core operators define a multi-agent spatial-temporal game where each player's action is constrained by opponent behavior and field geometry. Blocking satisfies a temporal constraint (t_block), while advancing satisfies a positional constraint (x_runner - x_tackler). Interference expansion extends the play through repositioning, modeled as a probabilistic continuation. These form a closed-loop system: constraints propagate through time and space, with feedback from outcome metrics. Failure modes include t_block < t_breach (early disruption), x_runner - x_tackler < threshold (collision), and T_rejoin > T_threshold (loss of momentum). The dualities lie in the symmetry between blocking and advancing roles, both requiring predictive timing and spatial awareness. Each primitive maps to a distinct layer in GSI’s Bayesian inference framework, where observables like force and velocity are transformed into probabilistic states. In GSE, these become state transitions in a dynamic programming model.
